cholesterol is transferred from vesicles to rat arterial smooth muscle in vitro and that the transfer is enhanced by bovine serum albumin.

cholesterol transfer between cells and vesicles is saturable, is influenced by the C/P mole ratio of the vesicle lipid and is enhanced by the presence of albumin.

the cholesterol transfer between cells and vesicles is not mediated via a specific carrier protein.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cholesterol transfer from vesicles to smooth muscle cells in our experimental conditions is a saturable, protein-dependent process, which may involve both the cell membrane cholesterol and the intracellular cholesterol pools.
cholesterol exchange between vesicles and smooth muscle cells is a rapid process, which can be enhanced by bovine serum albumin.
cholesterol exchange between cells and vesicles is a complex phenomenon, involving both the aqueous diffusion and the esterification of cholesterol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cholesterol exchange between cells and vesicles is a saturable process.

the cell membrane is a dynamic entity, and the cholesterol content of the cell membrane is not static, but can be altered by cholesterol exchange with other cholesterol pools within the cell and with cholesterol present in the surrounding medium.
the cholesterol exchange between the cell and the extracellular medium is a saturable process, which is enhanced by the presence of albumin.
